extracted.intended_audience: United States Indian Agents / Bureau of Indian Affairs officials
extracted.subtask_description: Standards and recommended practices for managing a U.S. Indian agency and composing its annual report (1880). Covers supplies, housing, education, agriculture, infrastructure, policing, medical care, and assimilation/land policy.

rubrics_metrics.name: Mission work effectiveness
rubrics_metrics.description: Mission work is conducted under the auspices of the Episcopal Church with the most satisfactory results, the clergyman in charge being an educated Santee Indian. Service is held in the agency chapel in Dakota and English.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Two resident missionaries exercised general supervision over the schools and conducted regular religious services; missionary supervision is presented as contributing positively to education and civilizing efforts.

rubrics_metrics.name: Police force organization and reliability
rubrics_metrics.description: The police force ... now consists of one captain, one sergeant, and eight privates. It is not efficient or reliable, and cannot be so when every man is equally well armed and reserves the right to be his own policeman.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Opposition and intimidation previously forced members to renounce service; reorganization is possible but effectiveness limited where each man is armed and claims to be his own policeman; little occasion yet to test the force.

rubrics_metrics.name: Subsistence supplies quality and delivery
rubrics_metrics.description: The subsistence supplies furnished during the year were abundant and of excellent quality. The beef was particularly good, and was plentifully and promptly delivered. Issues are made weekly on Saturday forenoon.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Weekly distribution schedule is recommended; quality of supplies (especially beef) should be monitored and contracts enforced; procurement inspection practices are described (see procurement/inspection standard).

rubrics_metrics.name: Agency infrastructure and facilities
rubrics_metrics.description: During the year the agency has been improved by the addition of a commodious issue house and two dwellings for employes... a new building 60 x 24 feet is being constructed of cottonwood lumber for blacksmiths', carpenters', and wagon shops, and the agency inclosure is being enlarged.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Provision of shops (blacksmith, carpenter, wagon), issue houses, dwellings, and saw-mill are important to agency operation and improvement; construction may be performed by employes/Indians when feasible.

rubrics_metrics.name: Staffing and employe composition
rubrics_metrics.description: The employes force consists of—whites: 1 physician, 1 clerk, 1 farmer, 1 carpenter, 1 blacksmith, 4 laborers. Indians: 1 interpreter, 1 chief herder, 2 herders, 2 laborers, 2 apprentices, 1 messenger.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Mechanical labor necessary to keep in repair nearly 200 houses, over 100 wagons, implements and machinery is very great and keeps mechanics incessantly employed; staffing must match maintenance workload.

rubrics_metrics.name: Reservation boundaries and land adequacy
rubrics_metrics.description: The present reservation should be enlarged so as to include the Yellow Medicine River or the lower part of it, and the Great Bend of the Missouri, where wood, water, and arable land may be found together.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Agent recommends enlargement because current arable land within reach of rivers is limited and will not be sufficient if land is taken in severalty; land access impacts settlement and subsistence.

rubrics_metrics.name: Encouraging permanent housing
rubrics_metrics.description: The log house, with dirt roof, is preferable in this country... The adoption of permanent abodes by these Indians is a very important step toward civilization, as it evinces a desire on their part to abandon their migratory habit of life and attach themselves to permanent localized houses.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Government aid has been limited to providing rough board doors, sash, hinges, and locks; encouraging log-house construction (and providing roofing/flooring when possible) will further settlement and civilization.

rubrics_metrics.name: Settlement dispersion and allotment policy
rubrics_metrics.description: They are settled, and are settling, at various distances up to 40 miles away. As soon as these Indians become house-owners and land-holders their glory as petty potentates will have departed.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Agent intentionally induced dispersion to promote family-level holdings; suggests that chieftainship influence declines as property is accumulated; implies policy support for allotting land to families and encouraging scattering.

rubrics_metrics.name: Stock-raising program preference
rubrics_metrics.description: The department, in June, 1879, issued to these Indians, as an experiment, 500 cows, heifers, and bulls, which was so successful... last June 1,000 head of native stock was purchased for them. The Indians have taken most excellent care of these animals... this would seem to offer the most feasible and practical method of making them eventually self-supporting.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Recommend repeated issues of stock cattle as a practical path to self-support; contrasts favorably with agriculture given climate and habit; monitor care and prevent slaughter of original stock.

rubrics_metrics.name: Agriculture feasibility and experimentation
rubrics_metrics.description: Agriculture, as compared with stock-raising, has its disadvantages considering the people, climate, and country... The past season was a decidedly bad one for crops, owing to lack of rain. I tried, as an experiment, oats and wheat on different parts of the reservation, and was much gratified with the result, as both grains headed and matured with a very good yield per acre.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: While experiments show some success (oats/wheat in places), caution that wheat cannot be grown remote from the Missouri; gardening and vegetables on stream bottoms may be productive; limited arable land and uncertain rainfall restrict large-scale farming.

rubrics_metrics.name: Education provision: boarding versus day schools
rubrics_metrics.description: There is a strong desire on the part of the Indians to send their children to school... the widely scattered location of the Indian houses necessitate the establishment of several day schools. Boarding-schools for their ultimate effect on the children are, of course, preferable to day schools.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Day schools are stepping-stones but boarding schools (remote from agency) are recommended to accomplish more; agent plans boarding-school capacity for 100 children and notes Carlisle training-school had salutary effect.

rubrics_metrics.name: Telegraph and communications
rubrics_metrics.description: Eighty miles of telegraph poles have been put up, and 20 miles of line put in operation by Indian labor. The line is now working between the agency and Camp Sheridan... expected that by joint labor the line will be in operation before cold weather.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Construction by Indian labor is encouraged; completing line connections between agencies and military posts is important to connect agencies with the outside world.

rubrics_metrics.name: Religious instruction and missionary oversight
rubrics_metrics.description: The Episcopal Church has kept two resident missionaries here, and these two gentlemen have done excellent work so far as their limited facilities would permit them. They have exercised general supervision over the schools, and conducted religious services on the regular days.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Missionaries are credited with positive influence on morals and education; their supervision of schools is part of the civilizing program.

rubrics_metrics.name: Chieftainship and tribal institutions abolition policy
rubrics_metrics.description: I believe that all the Teton Sioux should be disarmed and forced to receive and be governed by the laws or principles of law that govern the fifty million people who support them; that tribal sovereignty, chieftainship, the sun dance, all superstitious practices, and polygamy should be abolished by a prohibition by force; that each family should be allotted enough of arable land to live on... labor and education be made compulsory; that the sale and abduction of women be made punishable by imprisonment.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Agent states these changes can be effected only by physical force and acknowledges undoing some prior expenditures; this entry records explicit assimilation/compulsion policy recommendations and criminalization of certain practices.

rubrics_metrics.name: Supply management and preventing waste
rubrics_metrics.description: When I assumed charge of this agency, I found in nearly all the lodges from three to ten sacks of flour molding and becoming worthless... It was customary with the Indians to feed the same to their ponies... The authorized allowance of flour and corn to the Indian is one-half pound of each per day, and the beef allowance three pounds gross... I cut down the issue materially; likewise with the corn... Care on the part of the storekeeper has resulted in the saving in other articles.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Adjust rations to actual use, control issuance, prevent waste and misuse (e.g., feeding flour to animals), and employ storekeeper oversight to realize measurable savings to government and to teach value of supplies.

rubrics_metrics.name: Storage and waterworks infrastructure
rubrics_metrics.description: We are very much more in need of storage room, the building provided being entirely inadequate, forcing us to store many of the supplies out of doors. There is in process of construction, at this agency, a system of water-works for domestic purposes and protection against fire. The tank, of a capacity of 17,000 gallons, will be supported on trestle-work 30 feet above ground.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Adequate storage is required because year's supplies arrive at once; waterworks and elevated tanks, pumped by wind engine, are recommended for domestic use and fire protection.

rubrics_metrics.name: Medical services and decline of native medicine
rubrics_metrics.description: With the adoption of the white man's customs naturally comes the adoption of his system of medicine. The duties of the physician are on the increase, and the power of the native medicine man decreasing. The supply of drugs is ample in variety and quantity and of good quality.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Support and staff competent physicians; maintain ample drug supply; success of physician work encourages abandonment of quack/native treatments.

rubrics_metrics.name: Property maintenance: mills, bakery, and barns
rubrics_metrics.description: A saw-mill 82 by 24 feet was erected... The large saw-mill still remains in its original position inside the stockade... Authority has been granted to remove the mill and locate it convenient to timber and water. The bakery was nearly destroyed by a storm and will require large repairs. Material for a barn 40 by 120 feet... has been gotten out.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Collect, repair, and adapt existing machinery (mill converted to saw where needed); relocate mills to practical sites (near timber/water); repair or rebuild bakery and construct barn to support agency needs.

rubrics_metrics.name: Promoting industry and provision of tools/shops
rubrics_metrics.description: Many of them now bring wood-work for their broken wagons and machinery (hewn out and shaped for the necessary repairs), of their own manufacture... I have always encouraged them, believing that sooner or later the government would be justified in erecting for them shops and furnishing them with suitable tools to make their own repairs.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Encourage manufacture and repair skills, loan agency resources (e.g., work-cattle), erect shops, and furnish tools to develop latent mechanical ingenuity and promote independence.

rubrics_metrics.name: Provision of household amenities (stoves)
rubrics_metrics.description: I am gratified to learn that the three hundred cooking-stoves with pipe, for which I estimated, have been allowed by your office. The stoves are intended for use in the Indian houses, and I have no doubt will prove a great aid in getting the Indian into the white man's ways, for civilization in cooking is certainly a part of the general civilization of a race.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Distribution of household appliances (stoves) is presented as practical aid to assimilation and improved domestic comfort.

rubrics_metrics.name: Procurement and inspection standards for beef
rubrics_metrics.description: The beef contract called for steers not over seven years of age, averaging during the summer months 850 pounds per head, and during the winter 800 pounds per head, in good, healthy, marketable condition, and for which the contract price paid was $2.68 per hundred-weight gross. The beef is all received, weighed, and branded in the presence of a military inspector, and whose certificate is requisite before payment can be made.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Strict contract specifications (age, average weight, condition), on-site weighing/branding, and third-party (military) inspection with certificate are required to ensure honesty and prevent fraud in procurement.

rubrics_metrics.name: Reporting and accounting of savings from issues
rubrics_metrics.description: Property returns for the quarter ending June 30, 1880, show that there were taken up as savings from the issues: flour, 100,000 pounds; corn, 50,000 pounds; rice, 12,000 pounds; sugar, 10,000 pounds; hard bread, 10,000 pounds; bacon, 10,000 pounds; coffee, 8,000 pounds; baking powder, 800 pounds; soap, 1,000 pounds, and tobacco, 200 pounds, representing in money a value of about $11,000, which amount is a clear saving to the government.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Maintain detailed property returns and quantify savings from improved issuance and storekeeper care; report monetary value of savings as evidence of efficient administration.
